text:
Anika: Heads-up — I merged the role-matrix refactor to staging earlier. It was meant to tighten viewer/editor differences but QA found the edit button showing for some viewer accounts. @Maya can you repro?

Maya: reprod quickly. Steps: create org -> invite user as Viewer -> open Project > Settings. Edit button is visible for that user. Screenshot uploaded to the thread (screenshot link). :thinking_face:

Kevin: looking at the auth logs. The backend eval logs show `perm_check(project.update)` returned false, then frontend gating still rendered edit button. Suspect a client-side fallback or stale feature flag.

Leo: frontend uses `rbac-v2-gate` flag + a heuristic fallback: `if (cachedPerm || isAdmin) showEdit()` — that `cachedPerm` can be `undefined` which effectively becomes truthy in our render check. Bad logic. Example snippet: ```js
const canEdit = cachedPerm ?? isAdmin;
if (canEdit) renderEdit();
```

Maya: yeah that matches what I saw. Some viewer sessions still had old cache entries from before role flip. Clearing local storage made the button disappear.

Anika: ok. Two concern vectors: 1) UI exposure (confusing/privilege surface) and 2) audit/KMS impact if someone actually edits things that should be blocked. We need to treat this as a vuln triage item.

security-bot: automated scan flagged `perm-fallthrough` on staging at 2024-10-14T08:12:17Z. Severity: medium. See ticket #SEC-478.

Kevin: checked audit logs for the staging org — I can see `perm-eval` entries but the audit rows for actual `project.update` calls are sparse because some older sessions skip server-side validation when hitting the UI-only APIs. That's the real bug: there were front-end-only calls that didn't re-validate on the server.

Sam: whoa — front-end-only calls that mutate? That's a no-go. Which endpoints?

Kevin: small set: `/api/ui/save-quick` and `/api/ux/notes` (legacy UX layer). They call the same underlying service but skip the `enforceRBAC` middleware in some codepaths.

Leo: this happened because the refactor renamed role constants and we accidentally added an alias in the UX layer. The alias mapping caused `isEditor` to be truthy.

Anika: action plan: (1) revert the staging deploy of the refactor (ops can revert commit), (2) patch frontend gating logic to use explicit boolean checks (`=== true`) and remove `undefined` fallthrough, (3) add server-side enforceRBAC callsite to the UX endpoints, (4) run audit log search for any suspicious `project.update` writes in the last 48h, (5) open vuln triage ticket and include KMS/audit artifacts.

ops-oncall: I can revert the staging deploy now (commit cf3a9b2). Reverting in 5m unless security asks to preserve for forensics.

Anika: preserve one staging instance for capture — Kevin, grab the server logs and produce a short replay. Also export KMS audit metadata for any API keys used during the window (we only need key IDs, not material).

Kevin: grabbing logs now. I'll also run `SELECT * FROM audit.events WHERE action='project.update' AND ts > now() - interval '72 hours';` and drop results into the ticket.

Sam: for the vuln triage, recommend we classify as P2 until we can confirm any real-data edits. Mitigation: add explicit deny default + tighten gating in the client and server. Also add a quick e2e that creates viewer user and asserts no edit endpoint returns 403.

Maya: writing repro test now — adding to `rbac-e2e` suite. Will push a failing test to the staging branch so CI blocks the roll-forward.

security-bot: triage ticket created: SEC-478 (owner: Anika). Related alerts: perm-fallthrough, rbac-coverage-missing.

Anika: assigning: Kevin -> logs + audit export, Maya -> failing e2e, Leo -> frontend patch, Sam -> e2e+policy PR, ops-oncall -> revert + preserve instance. I'll coordinate the vuln ticket. If we confirm real edits occurred, we'll follow incident response checklist.

Leo: PR incoming in ~30m with explicit checks. Will also remove legacy alias map.

Kevin: logs exported and uploaded to SEC-478. I included KMS key IDs for any API key ops used in the window, sanitized per compliance.

ops-oncall: reverted staging commit and preserved a single preserved instance at staging-rt-42 for Kevin. :white_check_mark:

Maya: pushed failing e2e and test repro to branch `rbac-staging-fail`. CI caught it as expected.

Sam: opened PR for the `enforceRBAC` middleware on the UX endpoints, link in the ticket.

Anika: good work team. Once PRs land, let's run a focused canary: create viewer, try edit, confirm 403 + audit log entry + KMS metadata preserved. Post results in SEC-478 and we'll close the staging incident. :thumbsup:

Kevin: noted. Will run canary after patches land.

security-bot: SEC-478 status updated -> in_progress.

Anika: closing loop here, ping me if anything unexpected pops up. Thanks all.
